story.iWant: to see elapsed time during recording and easily stop the recording
story.soThat: I know how long I've been recording and can end capture when finished
story.tasks: - Create RecordingTimer component (AC: 1, 2, 3) - Implement timer logic (AC: 7) - Add Stop Recording button (AC: 4, 8) - Implement show/hide logic (AC: 5, 6) - Implement stop recording action (AC: 9, 10) - Create IPC stop handler (AC: 10) - Update recordingStore (AC: 7, 8) - Implement time formatting utility (AC: 2) - Style component for dark theme (AC: 12) - Ensure smooth performance (AC: 11) - Write component tests - Integrate with existing UI - Manual testing

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: `RecordingTimer.tsx` component created as floating overlay during recording
Timer displays elapsed time in MM:SS format, updating every second
Timer positioned top-right of screen, non-intrusive but always visible
"Stop Recording" button integrated into timer component with red styling
Timer automatically appears when recording starts (isRecording = true)
Timer automatically disappears when recording stops
Duration state updated in recordingStore every second via setInterval
Clicking "Stop Recording" button triggers stopRecording() action in store
IPC handler calls RecordingService.stopRecording() and returns output files
Timer remains responsive and smooth (no blocking) during recording
Component styled consistently with dark theme and CapCut design

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification
doc.snippet: RecordingTimer floating timer display with stop button during recording. Shows elapsed time and provides stop control.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification
doc.snippet: RecordingTimer appears in step 7 of screen-only, webcam-only, and PiP workflows showing elapsed time. User clicks "Stop Recording" button to end capture.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification
doc.snippet: IPC channel 'recording:stop' with no request parameters. Returns IPCResponse with RecordingOutput containing file paths and metadata.

artifact.reason: Reference pattern for progress display component with timer/status updates, shows how to format time and display progress UI
Recording state management - needs updateDuration and stopRecording actions for timer functionality

node.package: React hooks for component (useState, useEffect for timer interval)
State management for recording state subscription
Stop icon for button (Square or CircleStop icon)

constraints.constraint: RecordingTimer must be floating overlay component (fixed position, high z-index)
Timer positioned top-right (standard recording indicator position)
Semi-transparent background for visibility over any content
Time format MM:SS (or HH:MM:SS if recording exceeds 60 minutes)
Update interval exactly 1 second (1000ms) via setInterval
Must clear interval on component unmount to prevent memory leaks
Stop button styled red (universal recording stop convention)
Component only renders when isRecording = true
Must not block UI or affect recording performance
Dark theme styling consistent with existing CapCut-inspired design

tests.standards: React component testing with @testing-library/react. Mock Zustand store and IPC. Test timer updates, button interactions, show/hide logic. Mock setInterval/clearInterval for controlled testing.

ideas.idea: Test RecordingTimer component renders with timer and stop button
Test component has fixed position top-right CSS classes
Test stop button has red background styling (check className or styles)
Test component returns null when isRecording=false
Mock setInterval, verify updateDuration called every 1000ms
Test stop button click calls recordingStore.stopRecording()
Mock IPC, verify 'recording:stop' invoked on button click
Test interval cleared on component unmount (verify clearInterval called)
Verify dark theme CSS classes applied (bg-black/80, text-white, etc.)
